thread:
Alice S: Quick sync — FinRegCo wants an EU-only POC. Key asks: EU-hosted model endpoints, customer-managed KMS, and a signed subprocessor list. They also want a routing fallback plan if EU capacity is exhausted. Can we confirm feasibility and timeline?
Ben SE: Yep we can do EU pinned deployments for the POC. Two notes: 1) customer-managed KMS requires Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) or Dedicated with KMS integration. 2) routing fallback -> we can implement strict route policy to avoid non-EU by default, but need an agreed DR fallback for failures.
Alice S: They asked for timeline. POC start in 3 weeks. Which option is fastest while meeting KMS ask?
Ben SE: Fastest path is Dedicated in EU (reserved capacity) + KMS integration. Private takes longer (network + infra approvals). Dedicated + KMS can be done in ~2 weeks if they accept our standard Dedicated contract and provide KMS credentials + network allowlist.
Claire Sec: From security: we need subprocessor attestation and confirmation of which telemetry/metrics are exported. Also clarify whether backups/replication ever traverse non-EU regions.
Dan Legal: We'll need to provide subprocessor list + DPAs. If they require an EU-only subprocessor footprint (no non-EU subprocessors), that's harder — our infra provider and some telemetry vendors may have global infra. We can provide contractual commitments and offer controls (e.g., encryption, limited telemetry).
Emma (Customer): To be explicit: must not process EU customer data outside EU except for failover under strictly defined conditions (we'll accept documented failover only). Also KMS must be under our control.
Ben SE: Proposed routing policy options for POC: 
- Option A: Strict EU-only (no failover) — simple config but no automatic DR; if capacity lost, requests fail.
- Option B: EU-preferred with documented failover to global standby region (only on manual approval) — ensures availability but needs legal OK.
- Option C: EU Dedicated + multi-AZ within EU with warm standby (no cross-region) — best SLA but higher cost.
Claire Sec: For KMS: Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via our KMS integration (we'll need key ARN/endpoint and to validate IAM roles). Private supports customer-hosted HSM. We'll provide an ops checklist.
Alice S: Pricing question from procurement: what's the delta for Option C vs Option A (POC pricing)? Also they asked if we can pause token billing during enforced failovers.
Ben SE: Rough numbers: Option A (EU-only POC) = baseline POC rate. Option C (Dedicated multi-AZ EU standby) = baseline * 2.2 (approx). Pause-on-failover — we don't currently auto-pause billing; we can set throttles and rate limits. Need finance signoff for manual credits.
Dan Legal: I'll draft the DPA + subprocessor appendix and include emergency failover clause that requires 2 approvers (customer + Redwood) before cross-border failover. That should satisfy GDPR risk teams.
Claire Sec: Action items:
- Provide subprocessor inventory and attestations (we can redact contact details) — I can assemble this by EOD tomorrow.
- KMS integration checklist and network allowlist — Ben will share.
- Routing policy choice and pricing addendum — Alice to confirm with customer which option.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: "Reminder: Dedicated EU pool provisioning requests take ~5 business days once contractual and billing are in place."
Emma (Customer): OK — we'll review Option B vs C with our infra team. Priority is KMS control and no automatic cross-border failover. Thanks all.
Alice S: Great — I'll send a short summary + timeline to Emma after we pick the routing option. Meeting scheduled Fri 09:00 CET to finalize. :calendar: 
Ben SE: I'll prepare the integration checklist and rough cost sheet before Fri.
Dan Legal: I'll start the DPA appendix draft and put it in shared drive; will ping for quick review.
Claire Sec: I'll attach the subproc list and telemetry map tomorrow.
Alice S: Perfect — closing this thread until Friday. :thumbsup:
